newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bourse tells 38 firms to meet listing rules.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bourse tells 38 firms to meet listing rules.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange on Thursday told 38 companies listed before it shut down during the civil war to meet listing requirements by December 21 or be crossed out.

"The Beirut bourse informs the shareholders of the companies that issued shares on Beirut's official market...before December 21, 1995...that the 12-month period to settle their affairs and meet the required conditions ends on December 21, 1996," chairman Gabriel Sehnaoui said in a circular.
"A company that does not settle its affairs by that date will be crossed from the list of companies listed in the official market of the bourse," Sehnaoui added.
The circular gave the names of the 38 companies.

Sehnaoui said investors would be able to trade on the bourse's over-the-counter market the shares of any Lebanese stock company whose capital was the equivalent of at least $100,000, after lodging an application and relevant documents.
The Beirut Stock Exchange re-opended in January after a 13-year closure during the 1975-90 civil war.
Nine shares of five companies are currently listed: Solidere, Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.

The companies named in the circular include Casino du Liban, elecricity company Kadisha, Compagnie Libanais de Teleferique, Compagnie Libanais de Television, Almaza brewer, ABC stores and assurance firms Union Nationale and Libano-Suisse.
